route: deposit column header = IRW item code, keyword-injectivity against the S3 questionnaire's Q6 a-h (self-describing-code exemption, checked rather than asserted); plus Step 5b route 9 response-frequency matching on the resp axis
evidence: Two axes, both re-run in verify_muir_2025_resilience_behaviours.R. ITEM axis: the IRW code is the S5 File column header verbatim (the processing script melts the named columns; no positional step), and each header's distinguishing keyword matches exactly ONE of the eight shipped item_text strings -- its own -- 8/8, 0 cross-matches over the 8x8 grid ('collaboration within' vs 'collaboration between', 'processes and procedures', 'Innovative', 'Communication was effective', 'leadership were supportive', 'staff demonstrated resilience', 'willingness to adapt'). Column numbering is contiguous with the questionnaire's own (cols 1-4 = Q1-Q4 demographics, 5-11 = Q5 a-g, 12-19 = Q6 a-h), so position and content agree. RESP axis (route 9): raw S5 labels vs live integers, all 24 item x level cells identical under Sometimes=3/Frequently=4/Always=5 -- e.g. item 17 supportive_leadership 2/3/65 raw vs 2/3/65 live, item 13 collabortion_between_units 2/21/46 vs 2/21/46 -- against 16 of 24 mismatched under the reversed coding. DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the item axis is a header-to-questionnaire keyword tie, not an independent statistical identification -- the paper publishes no per-item M(SD), so a hypothetical error inside the deposit's own headers would not be caught here; it says nothing about the transcribed instructions; and the resp axis is pinned only over the three levels respondents used, since Never=1 and Rarely=2 have no rows.

route: Route 1 (published per-item descriptive statistics, paper Table 1) plus self-describing source column headers for the one tied pair
evidence: Paper Table 1 publishes Mean(SD) for the seven 'Opinions about Organizational Response' components; against live per-item statistics, in the shipped order: 3.86(1.00) vs 3.857(0.997); 4.39(0.79) vs 4.406(0.773); 4.81(0.57) vs 4.814(0.572); 4.73(0.64) vs 4.729(0.635); 4.64(0.68) vs 4.638(0.685); 4.67(0.68) vs 4.667(0.679); 4.73(0.64) vs 4.729(0.635). Largest mean deviation 0.016, largest SD deviation 0.017 over 7 items. Five of the seven are pinned outright by the mean alone (spread 3.86 to 4.81). Components 4 and 7 tie exactly at 4.73(0.64), so the statistics alone leave that one pair interchangeable; it is separated by the source column headers, which name their own content -- '8_opinion_actions_effective' against '...in response to the COVID-19 pandemic were effective' and '11_opinion_resilience' against 'MBRU exhibited sufficient resilience...' -- and those headers ARE the live item codes (the script melts them unrenamed). What this does NOT establish: the option_text-to-resp direction, which comes from the processing script's explicit OPINION_MAP and the questionnaire matrix column order, not from any statistic; and it does not test the transcribed instructions, which have no counterpart in the response data. Re-runnable as verify_muir_2025_resilience_opinions.R (VERDICT: PASS).

Step 5b exempt: mapping_basis=data_labels. The source file's own variable-description sheet ties each item code to its text directly (Inhibition1/2/3 -> wait-for-treat / middle cup / leash), and the processing script melts those column names through unchanged, so no positional inference occurs.
